brief: This filament rack is already built: four spool bays, each with a spool axle across it, and open bins on the pillar tops. Do not change the parts. Dress it for use: a filament spool hanging on every axle, and a few small printing tools in the open top bins.

requirements.requirement: Do not change the existing parts of the rack
requirements.evidence: No placed parts were added, removed or replaced; the build still has the same 110 parts (4 axles, 8 rod accessories, 9 bins, 36 caps, 16 notches, 19 pieces, etc.). Only props were added.

requirements.requirement: A filament spool hanging on every axle
requirements.evidence: hang_spools placed filament-spool props 1-4 on axle:2#0,0#5, 2#0,2#5, 2#0,4#5 and 2#0,6#5 (at y≈182 mm, z 200/531/863/1194); no prop warnings.

requirements.requirement: A few small printing tools in the open top bins
requirements.evidence: Top bins bin:0,0,2 and bin:0,2,2 (level 2, div3 compartments) hold a screwdriver (prop:7, stood upright in the front-left compartment) and a hand file (prop:6, stood in the bin at 0,2,2). The tweezers and hex-driver/hex-key-set I tried were refused or hid below the rim (PROP_BELOW_RIM) and were removed. So two tools are in the top bins, not a full set; the screwdriver and file are workshop tools, the catalog has no printing-specific small tool besides the spool.
check_build: ok, meshClash clear, no prop warnings. Only info-level OPEN_CAP_FACE note, which I left alone since the brief said not to change parts.

finish.summary: The existing rack is unchanged. Four filament spools hang on the four spool axles, and a screwdriver and a hand file stand in the level-2 open top bins. The mesh check is clear and no prop warnings remain. The tool requirement is only partly met: the catalog has few small printing tools, and tweezers and the hex tools were either refused or too short for the bin compartments, so I used the screwdriver and file instead.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
